Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

Class SavedSessions

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.ui.files.SavedSessions
public final class SavedSessions extends Object
An ordered, name-unique list of saved connection profiles ("sessions") for a file-style connector, plus the last local/remote directory each one was left in — the WinSCP/MobaXterm "quick connect to a server and land where I was" behaviour. Pure and JavaFX-free so it is unit-testable; persistence is a line-per-session key=value format loaded/saved via load(java.nio.file.Path)/save(java.nio.file.Path). Mirrors the pure-helper style of PathBookmarks and FileOrder.

Passwords are deliberately never stored. A session carries only the non-secret coordinates (host/port/user, an optional private-key path, and protocol flags), so the file is safe to sit in the user's home directory; quick-connect pre-fills everything but the password.

  • Method Details

    • add

      public SavedSessions add(SavedSessions.Session session)
      Adds session, or replaces the existing one with the same name (names are unique and compared case-insensitively, since they are user-facing labels). A session with a blank name is ignored. Returns this for chaining.

    • remove

      public boolean remove(String name)
      Removes the session called name, if present. Returns true when one was removed.

    • find

      public Optional<SavedSessions.Session> find(String name)
      The session called name, if saved.

    • rememberDirs

      public boolean rememberDirs(String name, String localDir, String remoteDir)
      Records the directories the panes were left in for the session called name, leaving the rest of the profile untouched. A no-op when no such session is saved, so callers can record unconditionally on disconnect without first checking. Returns true when a session was updated.

    • parse

      public static SavedSessions parse(String text)
      Parses the serialize() format. Unknown keys are ignored and a line without a usable name is skipped, so a file written by a newer build (or hand-edited) degrades rather than failing to load.
